case_number: Civil Appeal No. 3613 of 2022 (Arising Out of SLP (C) No. 21948 of 2019)

parties.respondent: State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr.

summary: The appeal challenged the Allahabad High Court's order upholding disciplinary action against judicial officer Muzaffar Husain for misconduct during land acquisition cases. The Enquiry Officer found charges 1–11 proved, leading to a 90% pension curtailment, later reduced to 70% by the High Court. The appellant argued charges were time-barred and legally untenable, claiming no misconduct as enhanced compensation was based on market value and upheld in other cases. Respondent contended that the Full Court's collective conscience was shaken and the inquiry was fair. The Supreme Court emphasized high standards of judicial integrity, referencing public trust and ethical conduct, while examining whether the punishment was proportionate and legally sustainable.
legal_provisions_cited: Rule-3 of U.P. Govt. Servants Conduct Rules, 1956
Article 351(A) of the Civil Services Regulations
Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894
Section 6(e) of the Transfer of Property Act
Union of India vs. K.K. Dhawan
C. Ravichandran Iyer Vs. Justice A.M. Bhattacharjee & Ors.
Sarvepalli Ramaiah (D) Tr. Lrs Vs District Collector Chittoor
Krishna Prasad Verma (Dead) Thr Legal Vs. State of Bihar & Ors.
Abhay Jain Vs. High Court of Judicature of Rajasthan & Anr.
final_judgment: The appeal was allowed in part; the Supreme Court upheld the finding of misconduct on charges 4–11 but modified the quantum of punishment, determining that 70% curtailment of pensionary benefits was excessive and reduced it to 50%, balancing accountability with proportionality in disciplinary action against a retired judicial officer.
